summary: AC1 and AC2 pass (call order and echo messages verified by code review). AC3 and AC4 fail due to a critical ORM cache invalidation bug.

The doSeedTests() call sequence is correct, but the seeder cannot complete successfully because truncateAllTables() wipes the database without resetting the ORM collection caches (BaseCollection::$records and ::$idLookup). After the bootstrap authenticates user ID 1, the Users collection caches the record. When truncateAllTables() runs, the DB row is wiped but the cache retains idLookup[1]=true and records[1]. When seedSystemUsers() runs, initSystemUser(user 1) calls idExists(1) which returns true (stale cache), takes the UPDATE branch, finds no changes (cached values match), and never re-inserts user 1 into the DB. On any subsequent run, the bootstrap finds no user ID 1 and fails.

AC3 (single run) is conditionally verified: with user 1 pre-seeded the first call to composer seed-tests outputs '- Seeding test database... DONE.' But this requires an externally pre-seeded DB; the seeder itself leaves user 1 missing after run.
AC4 (idempotency) fails: second run of composer seed-tests crashes with 'Record data not found for user ID 1' because user 1 was not re-created during the first run due to the cache bug.
PHPStan: 0 errors. Regression tests: DBHelper 83/83 pass, Countries 56/56 pass, Locale 9/9 pass.

comments.note: CRITICAL: truncateAllTables() does not invalidate ORM collection caches. After bootstrap authenticates user ID 1, BaseCollection::$records[1] and ::$idLookup[1]=true are populated. After truncation the DB row is gone but idExists(1) returns true from cache. seedSystemUsers() → initSystemUser(user 1) takes the UPDATE branch (user 'exists' per cache), finds no changed values, and silently skips re-inserting user 1 into the DB. Fix: call AppFactory::createUsers()->resetCollection() (and AppFactory::createCountries()->resetCollection() for safety) after truncateAllTables() in doSeedTests(), or in truncateAllTables() itself.

SECONDARY (related): composer seed-tests fails on a completely empty DB because the bootstrap init() calls createEnvironment() → authenticateUser() → session->runAuthentication() → getSystemUser() (user ID 1) before doSeedTests() runs. The APP_SEED_MODE flag only skips configureUsers() but does not prevent the session authentication from querying user ID 1. The plan explicitly states the new setup flow is: import schema-only SQL → run composer seed-tests. This requires the bootstrap to handle an empty known_users table gracefully when APP_SEED_MODE is defined. Fix: in TestSuiteBootstrap._boot(), also guard createEnvironment() with !defined('APP_SEED_MODE'), or in Session/Base::runAuthentication() return a null/ghost user when APP_SEED_MODE is defined.

The Countries collection may have the same ORM cache staleness issue as Users: if countries were loaded during bootstrap they would be cached in AppFactory::createCountries(). The isoExists() guard in seedCountries() could return stale 'true' results, causing countries to be silently skipped. After fixing the Users cache issue, verify seedCountries() also resets its collection or uses DB-direct checks.

No automated test validates the end-to-end doSeedTests() outcome — that the DB contains exactly the expected rows after seeding. A unit test or integration test that calls TestSuiteBootstrap::doSeedTests() (with proper setup) and asserts row counts would catch these issues automatically.

Bug 1 (ORM cache after truncation): `doSeedTests()` now calls `AppFactory::createUsers()->resetCollection()` and `AppFactory::createCountries()->resetCollection()` after `truncateAllTables()` to invalidate any stale in-process ORM caches.

comments.note: `doSeedTests()` explicitly enumerates `AppFactory::createUsers()->resetCollection()` and `AppFactory::createCountries()->resetCollection()`. The inline comment explains the rationale clearly. The coupling concern is that a future seeder addition (e.g. `seedRoles()`) would require a developer to remember to add a matching `resetCollection()` call here. Consider adding a note to the `doSeedTests()` docblock naming this as a maintenance obligation, or extracting a `resetSeedCollections()` helper on `TestSuiteBootstrap` when the seeder grows.

The two separate `if(!defined('APP_SEED_MODE'))` blocks in `_boot()` are functionally correct and the split around `configureDatabase()` + `registerTransactionCleanupHandler()` is intentional (those always run). The pattern is readable but if `APP_SEED_MODE` guarding ever spreads to additional bootstrap methods, introducing a private `isInSeedMode(): bool` helper would improve discoverability and allow IDE rename refactoring.

No observations beyond the two notes above — implementation is clean, well-commented, and consistent with project conventions. notes: QA FAIL — bounce to Developer. Two bugs must be fixed before AC3 and AC4 can pass.

Bug 1 (CRITICAL): truncateAllTables() does not reset ORM caches. After truncation, BaseCollection::$records[1] and ::$idLookup[1]=true are stale. seedSystemUsers() detects user 1 as 'existing', skips re-insert, and user 1 is missing from DB after every seed run. Fix: call AppFactory::createUsers()->resetCollection() (and AppFactory::createCountries()->resetCollection()) after truncateAllTables() in doSeedTests().

Bug 2 (SECONDARY): On a schema-only empty DB, the bootstrap fails before doSeedTests() runs because session->runAuthentication() calls getSystemUser() (user ID 1) even when APP_SEED_MODE is defined. The plan's intended workflow requires this to work. Fix: guard the getSystemUser() call in Session/Base::runAuthentication() with !defined('APP_SEED_MODE'), or skip createEnvironment() in TestSuiteBootstrap._boot() when APP_SEED_MODE is defined.
